questions.question: The estimation of the volume fraction of the second phase (V<sub>i</sub>) by equating it to A<sub>i</sub>/A<sub>t</sub> real analysis where A<sub>i</sub> is the area of the second phase, and A<sub>t</sub> is the total area is called :

explanations.a: Correct — Areal analysis estimates volume fraction by measuring the area fraction (Ai/At) of a phase in a 2D micrograph, assuming it represents the 3D volume fraction.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Lineal analysis is based on line intercept methods, not direct area measurement.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Point counting estimates volume fraction by counting the number of points falling on a phase, not by measuring area directly.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Asymmetric analysis is not a standard method in quantitative metallography.

questions.question: The estimation of the volume fraction of the second phase (V<sub>i</sub>) by equating it to L<sub>i</sub>/L<sub>t</sub> where L<sub>i</sub> is the line-intercept length of the second phase, and L<sub>t</sub> is the total length of  measurement is called :

explanations.a: Incorrect — areal analysis is based on area fraction (Ai/At), not line intercept measurements.
explanations.b: Correct — lineal analysis uses the ratio Li/Lt based on line-intercept lengths to estimate volume fraction of phases in stereology.
explanations.c: Incorrect — point counting uses number of points falling on a phase, not line intercept lengths.
explanations.d: Incorrect — asymmetric analysis is not a standard method in quantitative metallography.

questions.question: The estimation of the volume fraction of the second phase (V<sub>i</sub>) by equating it to P<sub>i</sub>/P<sub>t</sub>where P<sub>i</sub> is the number of points falling on second phase, and P<sub>t</sub> is the total number of points is called :

explanations.a: Incorrect — areal analysis is based on area fraction (Ai/At), not point ratios.
explanations.b: Incorrect — lineal analysis is based on line intercept lengths (Li/Lt), not point counting.
explanations.c: Correct — point counting method estimates volume fraction using the ratio Pi/Pt, where Pi is points on the phase and Pt is total points.
explanations.d: Incorrect — asymmetric analysis is not a standard method in quantitative metallography.

questions.question: Using lineal analysis, the drawn lines :

answers.a: must be parallel to horizontal direction
answers.b: must be perpendicular to vertical direction
answers.c: must be equal in horizontal and vertical direction
answers.d: must not be in any order

explanations.a: Incorrect — lines in lineal analysis are not restricted to only horizontal direction; such restriction would introduce bias.
explanations.b: Incorrect — there is no requirement that lines must be perpendicular to vertical direction specifically; orientation should not be fixed.
explanations.c: Correct — in lineal analysis, lines are typically drawn in multiple orientations (both horizontal and vertical, often random or equally distributed) to avoid directional bias.
explanations.d: Incorrect — lines should not be completely random without control; a systematic or isotropic sampling approach is required for reliable results.

questions.question: Find the FALSE statement, Quantitative metallography of reporting volume fraction of second phase :

answers.a: False — volume fraction obtained from quantitative metallography is an estimate, not an exact “actual” value of the material due to sampling and statistical limitations.
answers.b: True — values may slightly differ depending on areal, lineal, or point analysis because each method has statistical variability.
answers.c: True — results are statistical in nature and accuracy improves with more measurements or data points.
answers.d: True — volume fraction can be deduced from stereological principles relating 2D measurements to 3D structures.
